category: S3-compatible object storage, NVMe SSD class in 1-AZ regions

free_tier.stated: No free tier: the High Performance class in a 1-AZ (One Zone) region is billed from the first GiB at USD 0.00002778 per GiB-hour (about USD 0.0202794 per GiB-month), with no capacity cap stated
free_tier.notes: billed per GiB-hour; the monthly figure is the hourly price x 730 hours

per_object_cap.stated: 48 TiB per object through multipart upload; 5 GiB through a single PUT
per_object_cap.notes: the Object Storage technical limits page states one set of limits for the Object Storage offer

retention.stated: unlimited volume and time: objects are kept until deleted, and the High Performance class has no minimum storage duration
retention.notes: the price table marks the High Performance minimum storage billed N/A

egress.terms: External ingoing and outgoing traffic, internal traffic, data retrieval and API requests are all free

tooling: AWS CLI, rclone, s3cmd, any S3 SDK; lifecycle rules move objects between classes
chaining: S3 origin behind a CDN or proxy; lifecycle rules move objects between this class and the Standard class

limits.value: 48 TiB per object by multipart upload; 5 GiB by a single PUT
300 PUT and 900 GET requests per second per bucket, soft defaults

limits_note: Single availability zone: 99.9% availability SLA; not offered in the 3-AZ regions or in Local Zones
binding_note: none: storage has no stated cap, an object may reach 48 TiB, the per-bucket rates of 300 PUT and 900 GET requests per second are soft defaults, and the 1 Gbps per connection is lifted by parallel connections

identity_cost.detail: an email address validated by a one-time code, the country of tax residence, and a valid payment method on the account before the first Public Cloud project

reliability_note: 99.9% availability SLA for a 1-AZ deployment; durability is stated as 11 nines for every class
confidence_note: documented: the international price list, the storage classes pages, the endpoints page and the technical limits page were read and quoted on 2026-11-03; a read timed from a bucket would make it measured
